endorsements.quote: In practice: treat prompts as living methodological assets. Version-control them, test them systematically across inputs, and document how outputs vary.
Treating data work as scientific work, investing in metadata standards, ontology alignment, provenance tracking, and systematic bias auditing, is therefore not administrative overhead.

In practice: establish a minimum explainability standard before any model result is acted upon. This means: identifying the top predictive features and verifying they are biologically plausible; testing performance on at least one external cohort; and reporting a confidence or uncertainty metric alongside every prediction.

Familiarity with the Act’s requirements, and with analogous frameworks in other jurisdictions, including the FDA’s evolving guidance on AI-enabled medical devices 44 , is now a practical requirement for anyone designing AI systems intended for clinical use in Europe or in markets subject to European regulatory influence.
AI-generated GWAS pipelines that automate stratification correction without expert verification of the population composition amplify this risk at scale.
Hence, it is important to continuously monitor model drifts and uptake protocols/frameworks accordingly.

unlisted_practices: Stratify AI model performance by relevant subgroups (ancestry, age, sex, socioeconomic indicators) and report disparities as limitations before deployment.
Run a structured data audit for batch effects, class imbalance, missing metadata, and annotation inconsistency before any AI-assisted analysis, and document findings and corrections.
Continuously monitor foundation model drift and revalidate prompt libraries after model updates.
Write an implementation brief covering deployment requirements, stakeholders, validation and regulatory considerations for AI tools with translational potential.
Place computational biologists in clinical environments and clinicians in computational ones through cross-training programmes.
Involve bioinformatics experts in institutional AI decisions such as vendor evaluation, data infrastructure choices and training programme design.

screen.reason: Perspective/commentary on the evolving role and governance responsibilities of bioinformatics experts in the era of artificial intelligence.
